#### Course: Complexity Calculation

## Omega Mathematics

Now, let's see a mathematical example of Omega.

Example:

Given the following function,

```python
f(n) = 4n + 3
```

let's find c * g(n) based on the same conditions as before.

```text
f(n)≥c∗g(n)f(n) \geq c*g(n)f(n)≥c∗g(n)n≥n0n \geq n_0n≥n0​c>0c > 0c>0n0≥1n_0 \geq 1n0​≥1
```

Solution

Here,

The growth of the c * g(n) function won't be faster than the f(n) function after n0n_0n0​ because the above conditions are satisfied:

Since c * g(n) never grows faster than f(n) does, g(n) can be any expression such as 2n, 3n, etc. However, c * g(n) cannot be 5n, 10n, etc., because these functions grow faster than 4n + 3.

Let's assume c * g(n) is 2 * n. In this scenario,

```text
c∗g(n)=2∗nc * g(n) = 2 * nc∗g(n)=2∗nf(n)=4n+3f(n) = 4n + 3f(n)=4n+3Since, c∗g(n) cannot grow faster than f(n)Since,\ c * g(n)\ cannot\ grow\ faster\ than\ f(n) Since, c∗g(n) cannot grow faster than f(n)4n+3≥2n [for all n≥1]4n + 3 \geq  2n\ [for\ all\ n \geq 1]4n+3≥2n [for all n≥1]
```

![Omega Example](data:image/png;base64,)

As c * g(n) <= f(n) we can say that:

```python
f(n) = Ω(g(n))
=> f(n) = Ω(n) [read as f(n) is Omega of n]
```

Additionally, we could have chosen c * g(n) to be 3n or logn as well, because these functions also don't grow faster than 4n + 3.
